<system-reminder>
Consider calling `todo` first to lay out a phased plan with a single `init` op. A good list covers the whole request — investigation through implementation and verification — not just the next step, with specific task descriptions a future turn could execute without re-planning.
A useful list keeps each task to a concise, specific 5-10 word label; the `init` op only accepts phase names and task-label strings, so don't invent extra task metadata fields.
If you create the list, continue the request in the same turn and avoid re-calling `todo` unless task state materially changes.
</system-reminder>

# Run from ~/sovereign/projects/tau
{
  echo "=== GIT ==="
  git branch --show-current
  git log -1 --format='%h %s'

  echo; echo "=== TOP LEVEL ==="
  ls -la

  echo; echo "=== WORKSPACE DECLARATION ==="
  [ -f package.json ]       && jq '{name, workspaces, packageManager}' package.json
  [ -f pnpm-workspace.yaml ] && cat pnpm-workspace.yaml
  [ -f lerna.json ]          && cat lerna.json
  [ -f turbo.json ]          && cat turbo.json

  echo; echo "=== EVERY PACKAGE.JSON (path | name | version) ==="
  find . -name package.json \
    -not -path '*/node_modules/*' -not -path '*/.git/*' \
    -not -path '*/dist/*' -not -path '*/.tau/*' \
    -not -path '*/.cache/*' -not -path '*/build/*' \
  | sort | while read -r p; do
      printf '%-70s | %-40s | %s\n' \
        "$p" \
        "$(jq -r '.name // "?"' "$p" 2>/dev/null)" \
        "$(jq -r '.version // "?"' "$p" 2>/dev/null)"
    done

  echo; echo "=== DIR SKELETON (depth 3, filtered) ==="
  find . -maxdepth 3 -type d \
    -not -path '*/node_modules*' -not -path '*/.git*' \
    -not -path '*/dist*' -not -path '*/.tau*' \
  | sort

  echo; echo "=== LAUNCHER ==="
  sed -n '1,60p' ~/.local/bin/tau 2>/dev/null
  ls -la launcher/ 2>/dev/null
} > /tmp/tau-fingerprint.txt

wc -l /tmp/tau-fingerprint.txt
